description.narrative: Faris Al-Arab Foundation will lead the full implementation cycle, including worker identification, placement, supervision, monitoring, and reporting, while Oxfam will manage the direct wage payments to the workers, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and fiduciary standards. The CfW workers will be deployed across a broad range of activities that respond to identified community and sector needs, including community-driven interventions (light rehabilitation of shared community assets, environmental cleaning campaigns, support to service delivery organizations, and other community initiatives identified through participatory needs assessments),agricultural and non-agricultural productive sectors, and — as a particular area of focus — placement within existing agricultural nurseries operating in the Gaza Strip that are currently active and in need of additional labour to sustain and expand their operations. Priority will be given to nurseries and other productive activities that are already operational and where CfW placement can deliver an immediate contribution to ongoing production, rather than to activities requiring new setup or long lead times. The nomination process will follow three distinct tracks depending on the placement type: for placement in nurseries, workers will be nominatedby the nursery owners themselves, prioritizing workers who lost their income due to the current situation; for placement in other productive sectors, workers will be nominated by the enterprise owners, focusing on workers who were laid off due to the war and whose reintegration would also help enterprises scale up their production, alongside supporting the existing workforce; for community-based initiatives, a public call will be issued to attract workers fromthe same target communities. Final selection across all three tracks will apply CWG Palestine targeting standards, with priority given to women-headed households, young people (aged 18–35), and members of the wider vulnerable population identified through vulnerability scoring. Faris Al-Arab Foundation will ensure compliance with CWG Palestine standards, safe working conditions, and appropriate matching of workers to placement opportunities based on skills, location, and needs.

participating-org.narrative: Fares Al Arab for Development & Cha

Fares Al Arab for Development <(>&<)> Charity Works (FAFD) is a Palestinian non-profit, non-governmental organization established in 2006 and registered with the Palestinian Ministry of Interior under license number (7314). The organization operates across theGaza Strip and works to enhance the resilience and well-being of vulnerable communities through humanitarian response and sustainable development interventions.
FAFD implements programs focusing on women’s empowerment and protection, youth capacity building and empowerment, child protection, psychosocial support, and humanitarian response and relief. The organization adopts a participatory and rights-based approach, ensuring that its interventions promote gender equality, community engagement, and equitable access to services across diverse geographic areas.
FAFD has extensive experience collaborating with international and national partners in implementing humanitarian and development projects. Previous and current partners include UNDP/PAPP, the World Food Programme (WFP), Danish Refugee Council (DRC), the Palestinian Affairs Unit of the U.S. Department of State, Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Foundation, Pal-Think for Strategic Studies, the Palestinian Working Women Society for Development (PWWSD), the National Development Center (NDC), the World Bank, and Al Ahli Arab Hospital.
